mn72:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn72:2.1: Then Vacchagotta the Wanderer went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
mn72:2.2: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:
mn72:3.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—[^1]
mn72:3.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:3.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:3.4: ‘the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:4.1: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:4.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:4.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:4.4: ‘the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:5.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:5.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:5.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:5.4: ‘the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:6.1: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:6.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:6.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:6.4: ‘the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:7.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:7.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:7.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:7.4: ‘the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:8.1: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:8.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:8.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:8.4: ‘the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:9.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata is,[^2] only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:9.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:9.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:9.4: ‘after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:10.1: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:10.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:10.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:10.4: ‘after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:11.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:11.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:11.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:11.4: ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:12.1: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—
mn72:12.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?”
mn72:12.3: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:
mn72:12.4: ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”
mn72:13.1: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.2: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.3: the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.4: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.5: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.6: the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.7: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.8: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.9: the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.10: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.11: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.12: the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.13: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.14: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.15: the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.16: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.17: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.18: the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.19: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.20: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.21: after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.22: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.23: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.24: after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.25: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.26: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.27: after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.28: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—
mn72:13.29: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—
mn72:13.30: after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”
mn72:13.31: But what danger does Master Gotama see, that he is thus altogether disassociated from all these fields of view?”
mn72:14.1: ‘Vaccha, the view “the world is eternal” is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views; it is accompanied by suffering, by vexation, by despair, and by fever, and it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn72:14.2: The view “the world is not eternal” …
mn72:14.5: the view “the soul is the same as the body” …
mn72:14.6: the view “the soul is one and the body another” …
mn72:14.7: the view “after death a Tathāgata is” …
mn72:14.8: the view “after death a Tathāgata is not” …
mn72:14.9: the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” …
mn72:14.10: … and the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not” is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views; it is accompanied by suffering, by vexation, by despair, and by fever, and it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn72:14.11: It is seeing this danger, Vaccha, that I am thus altogether disassociated from all these fields of view.”
mn72:15.1: “But does Master Gotama have any view of his own?”
mn72:15.2: “‘View’, Vaccha, is something a Tathāgata has done away with.
mn72:15.3: For a Tathāgata has seen this:
mn72:15.4: ‘such is form, such its origin, such its disappearance;
mn72:15.5: such is feeling, such its origin, such its disappearance;
mn72:15.6: such is perception, such its origin, such its disappearance;
mn72:15.7: such are formations, such their origin, such their disappearance;
mn72:15.8: such is consciousness, such its origin, such its disappearance.’
mn72:15.9: Therefore I say that a Tathāgata is liberated through the exhaustion, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishment of all conceiving, all excogitation, all I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit, without clinging.”
mn72:16.1: “When a bhikkhu’s mind is liberated thus, Master Gotama, where does he reappear?”
mn72:16.3: “Then he does not reappear, Master Gotama?”
mn72:16.4: “‘Does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:16.5: “Then he both reappears and does not reappear, Master Gotama?”
mn72:16.6: “‘Both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:16.7: “Then he neither reappears nor does not reappear, Master Gotama?”
mn72:16.8: “‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:17.1: ‘“When a bhikkhu’s mind is liberated thus, Master Gotama, where does he reappear?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Reappears’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:17.2: “Then he does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:17.3: “Then he both reappears and does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:17.4: “Then he neither reappears nor does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”
mn72:17.5: Here, Master Gotama, I have fallen into unknowing, I have fallen into confusion,
mn72:17.6: and whatever small measure of confidence I had through Master Gotama’s earlier conversation has now vanished.”[^3]
mn72:18.1: “Enough of your unknowing, Vaccha, enough of your confusion.
mn72:18.2: This Dhamma is profound, hard to see, hard to discover, peaceful, sublime, unattainable by mere reasoning, subtle, to be experienced by the wise.
mn72:18.3: It is hard for you to know it since you hold a different view, favour a different acceptance, aspire to a different goal, undertake a different training, and follow a different teacher.
mn72:18.4: So then, Vaccha, I shall question you about this in return; answer as you see fit.
mn72:19.2: if a fire were burning before you, would you know:
mn72:19.4: “If a fire were burning before me, Master Gotama, I would know:
mn72:19.6: “If someone were to ask you, Vaccha, thus:
mn72:19.7: ‘This fire burning before you—what does it burn dependent on?’ Being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?”
mn72:19.8: “If I were asked thus, Master Gotama:
mn72:19.9: ‘This fire burning before you—what does it burn dependent on?’ being asked thus, Master Gotama, I would answer thus:
mn72:19.10: ‘This fire burning before me burns dependent on grass and sticks as fuel.’”[^4]
mn72:19.11: “If that fire before you were to go out, Vaccha, would you know:
mn72:19.12: ‘this fire before me has gone out’?”
mn72:19.13: “If that fire before me were to go out, Master Gotama, I would know:
mn72:19.14: ‘this fire before me has gone out.’”
mn72:19.15: “If someone were to ask you, Vaccha, thus:
mn72:19.16: ‘This fire before you that has gone out—which direction did it go from here:
mn72:19.17: east, south, west, or north?’ Being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?”
mn72:19.18: “That does not apply, Master Gotama. That fire burned dependent on grass and sticks as fuel, and with the exhaustion of that fuel, and no other being supplied, being without nutriment, it is reckoned as ‘gone out’.”
mn72:20.1: “So too, Vaccha, the form by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.
mn72:20.2: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of form, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,
mn72:20.4: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.

mn72:21.1: When this was said, Vacchagotta the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:
mn72:21.2: “Master Gotama, suppose there were a great sāla tree not far from a village or town.
mn72:21.3: Through impermanence its branches and foliage would fall away, its bark would fall away, its softwood would fall away;
mn72:21.4: and on a later occasion, divested of branches and foliage, divested of bark, divested of softwood, it would be pure and stand established in heartwood.
mn72:21.5: So too, Master Gotama’s teaching is divested of branches and foliage, divested of bark, divested of softwood, and it is pure and stands established in heartwood.
mn72:22.1: ‘Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyesight to see forms. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha. …
mn72:22.2: … From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.”
